title: Exposure-Response Tools for Time-to-Event Models
text: ertte time--event member exposure-response (E-R) package family, alongside erglm (GLM E-R models) emaxnls (Emax / logistic-Emax models), plug erplots visualisation. wraps survival::survreg()-based parametric accelerated failure time (AFT) modelling behind tidy, consistent interface: model fitting, AIC-based distribution selection, stepwise covariate modelling, simulation.

title: Fit an exposure-response time-to-event AFT model based on survreg() — ertte_aft
text: returned object class c("ertte_aft", "ertte_model", "survreg"): survreg object, little extra metadata attached. means usual survreg methods work unchanged, without needing ertte-specific equivalent – e.g. summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), predict(), AIC(), BIC(), logLik(), anova() comparing nested models. ertte_predict() separate, ertte-specific alternative predict() returns survival probabilities confidence intervals tidy data frame; two complementary, competing. ertte_aft() AFT-specific sibling ertte_coxph(), wraps survival::coxph() semi-parametric alternative. share "ertte_model" superclass, functions need generic operations (update(), anova(), SCM family) work unchanged across either engine; functions AFT-specific logic (e.g. ertte_predict(), ertte_fun()) dispatch via "ertte_aft"/"ertte_coxph" subclass. four supported distributions log-location-scale AFT models: log(T) = mu + scale * W, mu linear predictor (intercept + covariates) W follows distribution depends dist (extreme-value "exponential"/"weibull", standard normal "lognormal", standard logistic "loglogistic") – see ertte_predict() .ertte_dist_info().

text: returned object class c("ertte_coxph", "ertte_model", "coxph"): coxph object, little extra metadata attached. means usual coxph methods work unchanged, without needing ertte-specific equivalent – e.g. summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), predict(), AIC(), BIC(), logLik(), anova() comparing nested models. ertte_coxph() semi-parametric sibling ertte_aft(). title: Prediction function for an exposure-response TTE model — ertte_fun
text: ertte_fun() generic, methods supported engine – see ertte_fun.ertte_aft(). Named ertte_fun() consistency companion erglm/emaxnls packages' erglm_fun()/emax_fun(), serve purpose respective model classes. ertte_aft method takes fitted AFT model input returns function evaluates survival function S(t) user-specified parameters, data, times (e.g. VPCs counterfactual simulation scenarios). returned function checks param numeric one entry per column model matrix implied data, erroring informatively rather failing cryptic "non-conformable arguments" error matrix multiplication. scale always taken fitted object, param (coefficient vector coef() never includes ). ertte_coxph method returns function evaluates S(t | x) = S0(t)^exp((x - xbar)'param), S0(t) fitted baseline survival curve (via survival::basehaz(object, centered = TRUE), held constant beyond last observed time, matching ertte_predict.ertte_coxph()) xbar object$means (covariate means coxph() centers partial likelihood fitting – centering matters basehaz()'s baseline defined relative , x = 0). ertte_fun.ertte_aft(), param varies linear predictor: baseline hazard always taken fitted object, never recomputed hypothetical param (need refitting partial likelihood's risk sets) – matching level approximation used elsewhere package (e.g. scale AFT models likewise held fixed). Since Cox models intercept, param one entry per covariate "(Intercept)" column, unlike ertte_fun.ertte_aft().

title: Prediction function for an exposure-response TTE model — ertte_fun
code: mod <- ertte_aft(Surv(time, event) ~ aucss, ertte_data) mod_fun <- ertte_fun(mod)  # no arguments: reproduces the fitted model's own survival predictions s1 <- mod_fun(time = 60)  # user modifies the parameters par2 <- coef(mod) par2["(Intercept)"] <- par2["(Intercept)"] + 1 s2 <- mod_fun(param = par2, time = 60)  mod_cox <- ertte_coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ aucss, ertte_data) mod_cox_fun <- ertte_fun(mod_cox)  # no arguments: reproduces the fitted model's own survival predictions s1 <- mod_cox_fun(time = 60)  # user modifies the parameters par2 <- coef(mod_cox) par2["aucss"] <- par2["aucss"] * 1.5 s2 <- mod_cox_fun(param = par2, time = 60)

Nothing ertte_add_term()/ertte_scm_forward()/ ertte_scm_backward() prevents combining plain linear term (age) power term (ertte_power(age)) underlying variable – term handling throughout ertte works formula term-labels, variable semantics, left user's judgement. makepredictcall.ertte_power() stats::makepredictcall() method, typically called directly. ensures fitted model containing ertte_power() term used predict/simulate new data (via stats::model.matrix()/stats::model.frame() model's terms()), original fitting-time ref reused rather new one recomputed whatever data supplied – mechanism stats::poly()/splines::ns() use.

title: Survival-probability predictions for exposure-response TTE models — ertte_predict
text: ertte_predict() generic, methods supported engine – see ertte_predict.ertte_aft(). ertte_aft method computes linear predictor (standard error) via predict(object, newdata, type = "linear", se.fit = TRUE), converts survival probability S(t) = 1 - F((log(t) - mu) / scale), F base distribution's CDF implied object's dist (see ertte_aft() Details). Confidence intervals Wald intervals mu (qnorm() z-score times standard error), back-transformed way – parameter uncertainty scale propagated, matching level approximation used throughout package (e.g. erglm_predict()'s equivalent companion erglm package). conf_level must single number 0 1 (inclusive); values error rather silently producing reversed NaN interval. ertte_coxph method delegates survival::survfit(object, newdata, conf.int = conf_level), computes per-row survival curve S(t | x) = S0(t)^exp(lp(x) - lp(xbar)) fitted baseline hazard (Breslow Efron, matching object$method) linear predictor, evaluates time via summary(..., extend = TRUE) – extend = TRUE allows time exceed last observed follow-time, holding survival constant beyond (usual step-function extrapolation) rather erroring. Confidence intervals come survfit()'s conf.type = "log" transform (Wald log(-log(S))), better suited probability bounded [0, 1] plain Wald interval ertte_predict.ertte_aft() uses linear predictor – two methods' intervals directly comparable result, expected given different model structures.

title: Simulate from an exposure-response TTE model — simulate.ertte_model
text: Coefficients sampled asymptotic sampling distribution implied vcov(object). Event times drawn inverse-CDF sampling, via internal .ertte_simulate_draws() S3 generic, whose per-engine methods differ exactly : ertte_aft fits, directly fitted log-location-scale AFT distribution (see ertte_aft() Details); ertte_coxph fits, inverting fitted baseline cumulative hazard (survival::basehaz(), held fixed regardless sampled coefficient draw – simplification ertte_fun.ertte_coxph() makes user-supplied param). Simulated event times capped row's observed exit time (sim_time <- pmin(sim_time_raw, observed_time), sim_event set accordingly) reproduce study's observed censoring/follow-pattern – documented simplification, since true administrative censoring time subjects event otherwise available (see .ertte_simulate_draws()).
